en:
Check the schedule at the start of each
month. In J1 (Feb, Jul) and J2 (Feb),
you can also choose your tournaments.

This is this month's schedule.
Move the cursor to see details such as
the opponent for that day.

You can set up this month's schedule.
Choose from the tournaments or dates
to finalise this month's plans.

You can check last month's
fixtures and results.

Finish with this month's schedule.
Press the A Button if you are ready.
There is no match on that day.

Nothing is planned for that day yet.
Select from the list on the left to add
it to the schedule.

Adding this date will change a schedule
you have already set.
Is that OK?

Set up an overseas camp. The whole club
takes part and trains abroad for one
month.

Please select the region for
your overseas camp.

Attacking football built on individual
flair. Don't expect much tactically,
but physical growth looks promising.

Skill and style differ by country, but
this region values organised football.
Expect tactical and formation growth.

Known for attack-minded tactics. The
standard of individual skill is superb
so expect great growth.

Styles vary by country, but expect more
efficient training from modern methods
and gains from a keen attacking drive.

Unique rhythm and athleticism give
this country fine individual skill. It
should boost skill and physique.

Strong physiques and unusual individual
skill define this country. Its solo
breakthroughs stand out. Expect gains.

Famed for hold-up play that makes use
of its physical strength. It also has
real mental toughness.

Home to the world's strongest league.
Very defence-minded, they are the best
in the world at not losing matches.

Unlike the land of gentlemen, they live
for fierce football. Cutting attacks
from the wings overwhelm onlookers.

Renowned for organised attacking play.
The birthplace of modern football, so
expect to learn team play.

Individual skill is often highly rated
here. Expect gains in abilities such as
counters and free-kick accuracy.

A country famed for solid defending.
You can learn the mental strength to
grind out a win in any situation.

Europe's most attack-minded country.
Attacking structure and technique are
world-class. Expect better attacking.

Typified by fierce tackling and razor-
sharp counter-attacks. High balls and
rock-solid defence are strengths too.

Strong in midfield, with power and
skill. Good balance of attack and
defence, and high-quality goalkeeping.

Mental strength and leadership are
among Europe's best. The matches are
fierce, and the standard is very high.

Nordic physiques power its hold-up play
and fast counter-attacks. This country
has produced many miracle results.

It once produced many great players but
has slipped a bit lately. Basic skills
are high, so expect defensive growth.

Finishing is a mild concern, but their
ball skills are Europe's best. They are
known for developing midfield leaders.

Average by European standards. Strong
in both attack and defence, with the
attack especially outstanding.

Famed for high-level midfield play,
positioning and teamwork. Expect growth
in any position.

Perhaps mentally fragile, but highly
skilled, with imaginative midfielders.
Set pieces are well regarded too.

Individual technique is very high.
They can be a little hot-headed, but
play creative, imaginative football.

Physically gifted, with accurate and
dynamic football. Famed above all for
defence, so good for training keepers.

Pace and accurate finishing make this a
football power with a remarkably sharp
attack. Fierce play is another trait.

Money is tight at home, so the best
players leave, but this old football
power is known for strong attacks.

Unique style built on short passes that
prise the goal open. One of South
America's top nations.

The quality of its attackers is
striking. A good country for learning
goal sense and finishing.

Traditionally solid in defence. Attack
comes second, but organised, relentless
defending is South America's finest.

Skill on the ball speaks for itself.
Attackers show unrivalled flair and
imagination, and defenders attack too.

Known for strong defence. Sport enjoys
favourable conditions and scientific,
advanced training lifts basic ability.

Attack-minded, with defenders often
joining in. Even keepers join in, so
expect a more proactive attitude.

Please select the city for your camp.
The results of the camp depend on the
character of the city.

This overseas camp will cost
@P/$C@. Is that all right?

Arrange a one-off @Y/Preseason Match@.
You can choose the opponent, but there
is a cost if it is an overseas club.

The @Y/Platinum League@ for six of the
world's top clubs. You can enter if you
do well in the World Challenge Cup.

The @Y/Asia Tournament@, a contest for the
best club in Asia among 16 top clubs.

Take on the world's top 15 nations in
the @Y/World Club Tournament@.
Open the year after a J1 title.

The @Y/Europe Cup@, where 15 clubs from
Europe's top nations fight for the
crown. Asian Club League winners only.

The @Y/South America Cup@: 15 clubs from
its top nations fight for the crown.
Asian Club League winners only.

The @Y/World Challenge Cup@, gathering
clubs from all over the world.
Open to any club in J1.

The @Y/World Champions League@: six clubs
fight for No. 1. Open to winners of the
Europe Cup or South America Cup.

The @Y/Asian Championship@, against 15
Asian clubs matched to our strength.
Entry is for J2 clubs, apparently.

A @Y/Thanksgiving Match@ for supporters,
backed by our sponsors. Opponents
are chosen from around the world.

A one-off @Y/Friendly Match@.
You can choose the opponent.

The @Y/Asia Challenge Cup@ decides the
best country in Asia among the top 3.

A club that stresses developing hidden
potential. Known for attacking growth
and for building physical ability.

A top club focused on developing latent
potential. Expect big gains in physique
and defence, but attack is doubtful.

A club with an emphasis on developing
latent potential. Don't expect standout
gains, but balanced growth is likely.

Ideal for making a top-class passer.
A proven club that should also improve
understanding of many formations.

A traditional club to learn organised
football. Finishing is doubtful, but
midfield skills will surely improve.

You can expect growth in set pieces and
ball control. But don't expect much
from their shooting.

A prestigious German league club. You
can build defensive abilities. Even a
short stay should bring growth.

Ideal for learning rock-solid defence.
They should also return mentally
stronger and better in duels.

A club famed for dogged defending.
Expect gains in German-style mental
toughness and in leadership.

As the club that laid modern football's
foundations, many abilities can grow.
It also boosts 4-3-3 formation skill.

Known for building attacking basics.
Expect growth in attacking formations
and hold-up play at this club.

Expect balanced growth in attack and
defence. Training to extend potential
and a keen focus on young talent.

Many stars are on the books, so players
soak up all kinds of skills. Superb for
developing attacking midfielders.

A club that can develop well-rounded
players, solid in attack and defence.
It also brings out individuality.

A leading Italian power with one of the
world's most organised defences. Ideal
for developing defensive midfielders.

Builds a sense of the game around solid
defending. Also a good place to learn
elegant passing technique.

England's proudest and strongest club.
Famed for attacking down the flanks,
with strong growth in any position.

A great setting for building attacking
skills. Modern development methods give
ample growth even in a short stay.

Expect average gains in both attack and
defence. The zonal press is renowned,
but mental fragility shows.

Hard tackling shows aggressive football
is their creed. Expect big gains in
understanding 4-4-2 formations too.

Powerful attacks down both wings are
among the world's best. Recommended for
raising physically strong dribblers.

Astonishing attacking power is the core
of the Armada. You can also greatly
improve set-piece ability.

A relatively defence-minded club in the
attack-heavy Spanish league. Expect
balanced growth in attack and defence.

Nothing special as a side, but it could
be good for learning basic technique.
Don't expect big growth.

Expect great growth in left-wing attack
understanding. It should adapt to many
formations, but duels are a weakness.

A sit-deep-and-counter style of play.
Renowned for teaching defensive
formations. Good even in a short stay.

Seems well suited to basic technique.
Don't expect physical growth, but they
will come back mentally matured.

Dazzling dribbling through the middle
leaves defenders dizzy, a threat across
the north. Flexible formations too.

Long feeds that exploit gaps in the
defence are a real threat. Ideal for
polishing passing sense and dribbling.

A club famous for producing great GKs.
Known for tough training that drills
the needed skills in a short time.

Sharp reading and reflexes bring superb
save after save. They should produce
an impregnable goalkeeper.

An old Eastern European power famed for
its goal-denying defensive system. They
should bring out hidden abilities.

A club that gets the logic of winning.
Don't expect big ability gains, but
mental strength should improve nicely.

Known for technique at both ends of the
pitch. Little to gain tactically, but
it may unlock technical talent.

A club aiming for all-round growth in
technique and understanding. Balanced
training will develop utility players.

Picks up many skills, broad rather than
deep. Improves the basic skills needed
in every position across the board.

Broad improvement in basic ability is
expected, but outstanding growth in any
one area looks unlikely.

Expect a varied set of attacking moves
built on individual skill. They should
come back as a proud goalscorer.

Aggressive football with flair and
varied tactics. A dribbler's key
abilities should improve greatly.

Outstanding gains are unlikely, but the
basic attributes for attack should
definitely improve.

Typically Brazilian, strong in attack,
and built on individual skill. A good
fit for developing fast dribblers.

One of Brazil's top clubs. Soft touch
and fighting spirit are drilled into
players, so attack improves hugely.

Imaginative passing and mastery of all
tactics. A prestigious club to trust if
you want to improve attack.

A leading South American club. Skills
a speedy winger needs will grow a lot.
Don't expect much in defence, though.

A club with a very attacking style.
Tactical sense and hold-up play should
improve markedly.

Said to be unrivalled in Colombia for
solid defending. Success can awaken
defensive potential.

You can expect to pick up the basic
techniques of football. They may even
master elegant ball control.

Ideal for developing an aggressive GK.
Better free kicks are also a feature
of this club.

Don't expect notable gains in attack or
defence, but it may suit if you want
basic ability in a short time.

Very defence-minded, yet the full-backs
join attacks keenly too. That should
improve running and decision-making.

An old Central American giant that has
produced world-class GKs. Its methods
for training sharp-reflex GKs live on.

A young club, but its advanced training
methods for developing players are
watched by other clubs.
